podcasts.title: Export controls are only speeding up China’s chip self-sufficiency.
podcasts.summary: Export controls are only speeding up China’s chip self-sufficiency. “Starting this year, China’s self-sufficiency push has moved from state-led to coordinated between the toolmakers and the fabs themselves. They’re working together to design and build semicap equipment and EDA from the ground up, because what China needs could be different from the rest of the world, given its constraints.” “We believe this effort won’t be affected by export controls. In fact, as we’ve seen with China’s semicap localization rate over the past few years, export controls could accelerate it and give them more motivation to work harder.”

podcasts.title: ASML is bringing lithography-grade precision to hybrid bonding.
podcasts.summary: ASML is bringing lithography-grade precision to hybrid bonding. “BESI, ASMPT and others come from a pick-and-place background. They’re very good at overlaying each die onto the base wafer and placing it down. The bond itself forms later, during the anneal.” “ASML is coming at it from the front end. Its tools already do sub-nanometer overlay for lithography, easily an order of magnitude more precise. And as hybrid bond pitches get finer, how many signals you can fit per square millimeter between two dies matters more and more.” “Overlay isn’t ASML’s problem. The challenge is building a system that brings the dies to the wafer, or in this case, the wafer to the die.” Watch the Full Podcast on YouTube.

podcasts.title: Democratizing Security for the Agentic Web with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht
podcasts.summary: In the transition to the agentic web, security has become an afterthought. Now, organizations are racing to figure out what AI security means, and how to keep their data safe. Live from Cloudflare Connect, Sarah Guo sits down with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht to discuss the changing attacker landscape, and how his company is allocating its engineering resources to meet this emerging security challenge. Dane explains how enterprises that have moved away from castle-and-moat infrastructure to more of a zero trust infrastructure for security are in better positions than those who haven’t. He also discusses the challenges of patching 70 years of software and why the software development lifecycle will need to change for security for the agentic web, why he sees token spend in the next 18 months primarily going towards security rather than engineering, how the current web is in a ‘messy middle’ state where humans and agents are riding the same ‘rails’ on the internet, Cloudflare’s conference monetization gateway release as well as its Signals project with OpenAI, the rationale behind the release of Cloudflare OS, and the thinking behind a recent company restructuring. Plus, why Cloudflare hired one thousand interns, and why curiosity about AI is required to be successful at Cloudflare. Sign up for new podcasts every week. podcasts.title: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agents: Documents | Reducto’s Adit Abraham
podcasts.summary: AI agents can reason over enormous amounts of information, but much of the world’s actual work is still trapped in PDFs, spreadsheets, scans, and other formats that models struggle to reliably understand. Reducto co-founder and CEO Adit Abraham argues that solving this document layer is essential if agents are going to take on consequential work in healthcare, legal, finance, and insurance. Adit joins a16z General Partner Jennifer Li to explain why traditional OCR breaks down on messy real-world documents, how Reducto combines vision-language models with specialized infrastructure to reach high accuracy without sacrificing cost or latency, and why frontier models can silently drop information on long extraction tasks. Reducto now processes billions of pages each month, including its seven billionth page the morning of the recording. They also discuss Reducto’s R1 model, agents that can review and correct their own document extraction, and the company’s push beyond simply reading files toward letting agents reliably work with and edit them. Underneath it all is a higher-stakes problem: when a misread word can affect a healthcare claim or financial decision, getting the input right matters just as much as making the model smarter. podcasts.title: What Happens When Everyone Has a Health Expert in Their Pocket? | OpenAI’s Karan Singhal
podcasts.summary: More than 300 million people use ChatGPT for health and wellness questions each week. OpenAI’s Karan Singhal thinks that’s only the beginning: the longer-term goal is AI that can help people navigate their health proactively, while making trustworthy medical intelligence dramatically more accessible. Karan joins a16z Partner Jay Rughani to explain why OpenAI trains healthcare expertise directly into its general-purpose frontier models, how it works with hundreds of medical experts to evaluate safety and disagreement, and why the company sees AI as a complement to doctors rather than a replacement for medical care. They also discuss integrations with Epic, AI copilots for clinicians, and what happens as personal agents begin navigating appointments, health records, and other fragmented parts of the healthcare system. Looking further ahead, Karan makes the case that the cost of medical intelligence could continue to fall dramatically, allowing AI to act as a safety net for patients and clinicians, surface insights from years of health data, and potentially accelerate the discovery and validation of new treatments. podcasts.title: Building a Berkshire for the Middle Market – Tracy Britt Cool (EP.521)
podcasts.summary: My guest on today's show is Tracy Britt Cool, co-founder of Kanbrick, a long-term investment partnership that provides owners of family-owned, midsized businesses with a differentiated option from traditional private equity. Tracy launched the business after spending ten years at Berkshire Hathaway as one of Warren Buffett's few deputies. She started out of business school as a financial assistant to Buffett, served as Chair of several Berkshire portfolio companies, and later became CEO of Pampered Chef. Our conversation covers Tracy's journey, including lessons from Buffett and the value of operating experience. We turn to the application of those lessons at Kanbrick across its strategy, sourcing, deal dynamics, operational improvements, and long-term holding periods, all supported by the firm's creation of a community of 4,000 executives who share best practices in hiring, operations, excellence, and growth.
